- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% in those periods.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak observed in 3–5 day window.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to align with historical mean of last 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.2+), model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transitions to avoid false peaks.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 0.5–2.5% in 3–5 day window; apply 0.75–1.25% upward bias to 30d forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
